title: Forklift forklifts in construction study guide
description: Study guide on forklifts in construction: rated capacity, modifications, steering knobs, guards, riding, elevating personnel, training (29 CFR 1926.602).
intro: 29 CFR 1926.602(c) and (d) set OSHA's construction rules for lifting and hauling equipment (other than equipment covered under subpart N of 29 CFR Part 1926) and for powered industrial truck operator training. This guide sets out what the federal rule text states on posted rated capacities, modifications and additions, loads lifted by two or more trucks, steering knobs, overhead guards, riding on trucks, precautions for elevating personnel, and the note that the construction training requirements are identical to § 1910.178(l). Paragraphs (a) and (b), on earthmoving and excavating equipment, are not covered. goraedu does not train, evaluate or certify forklift operators, and a score here does not meet any training requirement. Your State may run its own OSHA-approved plan with its own rules, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

topics.name: Scope and rated capacity

points.text: Paragraph (c) of 1926.602 covers lifting and hauling equipment in construction, other than equipment covered under subpart N of this part.
points.quote: Lifting and hauling equipment (other than equipment covered under subpart N of this part).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Industrial trucks shall meet the requirements of § 1926.600 and the requirements listed in (c)(1).
points.quote: Industrial trucks shall meet the requirements of § 1926.600 and the following:

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Lift trucks, stackers, etc., shall have the rated capacity clearly posted on the vehicle so it is clearly visible to the operator.
points.quote: Lift trucks, stackers, etc., shall have the rated capacity clearly posted on the vehicle so as to be clearly visible to the operator.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When the manufacturer provides auxiliary removable counterweights, the corresponding alternate rated capacities also shall be clearly shown on the vehicle, and these ratings shall not be exceeded.
points.quote: When auxiliary removable counterweights are provided by the manufacturer, corresponding alternate rated capacities also shall be clearly shown on the vehicle. These ratings shall not be exceeded.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: Paragraphs (a) and (b) of 1926.602, on earthmoving and excavating equipment, are not covered in this guide.

topics.name: Modifications and loads lifted in unison

points.text: No modifications or additions that affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment shall be made without the manufacturer's written approval.
points.quote: No modifications or additions which affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment shall be made without the manufacturer's written approval.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If such modifications or changes are made, the capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals shall be changed accordingly.
points.quote: If such modifications or changes are made, the capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals shall be changed accordingly.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: In no case shall the original safety factor of the equipment be reduced.
points.quote: In no case shall the original safety factor of the equipment be reduced.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If two or more trucks working in unison lift a load, the proportion of the total load carried by any one truck shall not exceed its capacity.
points.quote: If a load is lifted by two or more trucks working in unison, the proportion of the total load carried by any one truck shall not exceed its capacity.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Steering knobs, guards and design

points.text: Steering or spinner knobs shall not be attached to the steering wheel unless the steering mechanism is of a type that prevents road reactions from causing the steering handwheel to spin.
points.quote: Steering or spinner knobs shall not be attached to the steering wheel unless the steering mechanism is of a type that prevents road reactions from causing the steering handwheel to spin.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The steering knob shall be mounted within the periphery of the wheel.
points.quote: The steering knob shall be mounted within the periphery of the wheel.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: All high lift rider industrial trucks shall be equipped with overhead guards that meet the configuration and structural requirements defined in paragraph 421 of American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969.
points.quote: All high lift rider industrial trucks shall be equipped with overhead guards which meet the configuration and structural requirements as defined in paragraph 421 of American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969, Safety Standards for Powered Industrial Trucks.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: All industrial trucks in use shall meet the applicable requirements of design, construction, stability, inspection, testing, maintenance, and operation as defined in American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969.
points.quote: All industrial trucks in use shall meet the applicable requirements of design, construction, stability, inspection, testing, maintenance, and operation, as defined in American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969, Safety Standards for Powered Industrial Trucks.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The content of American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969 is not described here; the rule only names it.

points.text: Unauthorized personnel shall not be permitted to ride on powered industrial trucks. Where riding of trucks is authorized, a safe place to ride shall be provided.
points.quote: Unauthorized personnel shall not be permitted to ride on powered industrial trucks. A safe place to ride shall be provided where riding of trucks is authorized.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Whenever a truck is equipped with vertical only, or vertical and horizontal, controls elevatable with the lifting carriage or forks for lifting personnel, additional precautions shall be taken to protect the personnel being elevated.
points.quote: Whenever a truck is equipped with vertical only, or vertical and horizontal controls elevatable with the lifting carriage or forks for lifting personnel, the following additional precautions shall be taken for the protection of personnel being elevated.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One precaution is use of a safety platform firmly secured to the lifting carriage and/or forks.
points.quote: Use of a safety platform firmly secured to the lifting carriage and/or forks.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Another is that means shall be provided so personnel on the platform can shut off power to the truck.
points.quote: Means shall be provided whereby personnel on the platform can shut off power to the truck.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A third is protection from falling objects, as indicated necessary by the operating conditions.
points.quote: Such protection from falling objects as indicated necessary by the operating conditions shall be provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Operator training

points.text: Paragraph (d) is headed Powered industrial truck operator training. Its note says the requirements for construction work under it are identical to those in § 1910.178(l).
points.quote: Note: The requirements applicable to construction work under this paragraph are identical to those set forth at § 1910.178(l) of this chapter.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The training, evaluation and certification content of § 1910.178(l) is not set out in this guide. Under that rule the employer trains, evaluates and certifies its operators; goraedu does none of that.
